recentItems.title: Tung Chee-hwa honoured with state funeral
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Hong Kong’s first post-colonial chief executive, Tung Chee-hwa, was honoured with a state funeral on Sunday. It was arranged by an 87-member committee chaired by Shi Taifeng, top vice-chairman of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) and a member of the Communist Party Politburo. The state funeral was only the third time a Hongkonger received such an honour since the 1997 handover.

recentItems.title: WATCH: State funeral for Hong Kong’s first chief executive Tung Chee-hwa
recentItems.description:
A public memorial and funeral ceremony is being held for Hong Kong’s first chief executive Tung Chee-hwa, with a farewell ceremony followed immediately by a funeral procession. The late leader is being honoured for his legacy as a deputy national-level leader and his contributions to the “one country, two systems” framework. Since the 1997 handover, only two prominent local figures have been granted state funerals: industrialist Ann Tse-kai in 2000 and tycoon Henry Fok Ying-tung in 2006. Both held the rank of vice-chairman of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC), a position that Tung also held.
Source:AP

recentItems.title: China’s Great Green Wall halts desert spread
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

China’s Three-North Shelterbelt Programme, otherwise known as the Great Green Wall, has significantly slowed the spread of the desert in the past decade. In 1998, China’s desertification zone totalled some 3.62 million sq km (1.4 million square miles), or a little over a quarter of China’s total land mass. Forests planted under the programme now span 500,000 sq km (193,050 square miles), increasing the area’s forest cover from around 5 per cent in 1978 to 14 per cent in 2022. Although the progress is promising, scientists warn the fight against desertification is far from over. They caution that preserving the gains will require decades of continued effort.

recentItems.title: Hong Kong bids farewell to Tung Chee-hwa in weekend vigil
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

A private vigil was held for Hong Kong’s first chief executive Tung Chee-hwa on Saturday at the Hong Kong Funeral Home in North Point, attended by high-profile figures including current Chief Executive John Lee as well as former leaders Leung Chun-ying, Donald Tsang  and Carrie Lam. Residents mourned Tung by signing public condolence books at several points across the city. The vigil took place one day before Tung’s state funeral, which is Hong Kong’s third since its 1997 handover from British rule back to China.

recentItems.title: Second chance at university degree for Filipino domestic helpers in Hong Kong
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

An NGO established in Hong Kong aims to give Filipino domestic workers a chance to obtain a bachelor’s degree through an accelerated education programme offered by the Philippine government. On Sundays, Hong Kong’s streets are filled with the sights and sounds of domestic helpers enjoying their days off. But many share stories of giving up dreams of earning a college education because they needed to support their families by finding jobs abroad as soon as possible.

Produced, written, filmed and edited by Jayson Albano.

recentItems.title: Three killed in Philippines school shooting
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

A teenage boy opened fire on his classmates at a school in Banga, a town in the southern Philippine province of South Cotabato, on Friday. He then took his own life. Two others were killed in the attack, and eight were injured. Authorities are investigating the shooter’s connection to an online group, according to the governor.

recentItems.title: Hyrox athlete apologises for Beijing soiling incident
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Hyrox competitor Joanna Wietrzyk apologised on social media on Thursday after being dogged by controversy following her win at the solo women’s event in Beijing on Saturday. Wietrzyk soiled herself mid-race but carried on competing, contaminating equipment and track surfaces. In her statement, she said she regrets not pulling out of the competition and that she will forfeit the points she earned.

recentItems.title: Japan’s ‘Suica penguin’ to be replaced in public vote
recentItems.description:
The beloved penguin mascot of Tokyo’s Suica transport smart card is set to be replaced when it retires early next year. Regarded by many as the most popular mascot in the country and beyond, the Suica penguin will be replaced by a new character. The new mascot will be selected from three contenders by public vote, set to conclude on September 23.

recentItems.title: Ex-Malaysian PM Najib given ‘conditional’ pardon
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Malaysia’s Pardons Board agreed Friday to allow disgraced former prime minister Najib Razak to serve out the remainder of his jail term under house arrest. King Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar granted Najib a “conditional pardon”, under which the former leader is required to settle his 50 million ringgit (US$12.3 million) fine before he can be transferred to his home to complete his sentence. Najib’s six-year term is set to end on August 23, 2028.

recentItems.title: Hyrox refunds athletes after Beijing soiling incident
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Hyrox China has issued full ticket refunds to affected participants after Australian athlete Joanna Wietrzyk soiled herself during the Beijing race on Saturday. Following intense public backlash, organisers apologised and updated the global rule book, allowing race directors to remove athletes on hygiene and contamination grounds.
